title: Probabilistic-bit hardware calibration at scale
bottleneck: Probabilistic computers use noisy p-bits for optimization and sampling, but each p-bit's randomness must be precisely calibrated and stable; device-to-device variation and temperature drift corrupt the probability distributions the algorithms assume. Scaling to millions of interacting p-bits while maintaining calibration is unsolved, and interfacing probabilistic cores with deterministic systems adds overhead.
why_it_blocks: Probabilistic computing could accelerate combinatorial optimization and Bayesian inference by orders of magnitude, but only if large p-bit arrays behave as modeled. Calibration drift turns a principled accelerator into an unreliable random-number generator.
current_state: MTJ-based and CMOS-based p-bit prototypes demonstrate small-scale probabilistic circuits. Million-bit calibrated arrays with stable statistics are still research goals. Temperature drift detunes p-bit statistics during operation, requiring recalibration schemes that themselves consume area, power, and design effort.
